meta_title: Tile Calculator - How Many Tiles Do I Need?
meta_desc: Free tile calculator. Enter your floor or wall size, tile size and grout gap to get the tile and box count with waste included. Instant, no ads.
og_desc: Get the tile and box count for your floor or wall, waste included. Free, no ads.
lede: Work out how many tiles and boxes you need for a floor or wall, with grout gap and waste included. Free, instant, no ads.
gap_hint_metric: 0 for no gap. 3 mm is common for floor tile.
perbox_hint: Printed on the box. Leave empty to skip.
how_text: The calculator divides your area by the footprint of one tile plus its grout gap, adds a waste allowance for cuts and breakage, and rounds up to whole tiles:
formula:
effective tile area = (tile width + gap) × (tile height + gap)
tiles = ceil( area / effective tile area × (1 + waste) )
boxes = ceil( tiles / tiles per box )
how_text2: Waste is 10% for a straight grid layout and 15% for diagonal or herringbone, where more offcuts end up unusable. A wider grout gap means each tile covers a slightly larger footprint, so the tile count goes down a little.
example_imperial: Say you are tiling a 10 ft by 12 ft floor, which is 120 sq ft (17,280 sq in), with 12 x 12 inch tiles laid straight and a 1/8 inch (0.125 in) grout gap. Each tile plus its gap covers 12.125 × 12.125 = 147.02 sq in, so bare coverage is 17,280 / 147.02 = 117.54 tiles. Add 10% waste: 117.54 × 1.1 = 129.29, which rounds up to 130 tiles. If the tiles come 8 to a box, that is ceil(130 / 8) = 17 boxes. The same floor laid diagonally at 15% waste needs 136 tiles.
example_metric: Say you are tiling a 4 m by 3 m floor, which is 12 m² (120,000 cm²), with 30 x 30 cm tiles laid straight and a 3 mm (0.3 cm) grout gap. Each tile plus its gap covers 30.3 × 30.3 = 918.09 cm², so bare coverage is 120,000 / 918.09 = 130.71 tiles. Add 10% waste: 130.71 × 1.1 = 143.78, which rounds up to 144 tiles. If the tiles come 11 to a box, that is ceil(144 / 11) = 14 boxes. The same floor laid diagonally at 15% waste needs 151 tiles.

faq: How much extra tile should I buy?

Buy 10 to 15% more than the bare coverage number. Cuts along walls, breakage and future repairs all eat into the extra. Use 10% for a simple straight layout in a rectangular room, and 15% for diagonal or herringbone layouts, small tiles, or rooms with many corners.

Waste is the tile you buy but do not end up walking on: offcuts at walls and around fixtures, tiles that crack during cutting or transport, and spares kept for later repairs. It is normal, not a mistake. This calculator adds the waste percentage before rounding up to whole tiles.
How many 12x12 tiles do I need for 100 square feet?

A 12x12 inch (30x30 cm) tile covers 1 square foot, so 100 square feet (9.3 m²) needs 100 tiles of bare coverage. Add 10% waste for a straight layout and you should buy 110 tiles. With a grout gap each tile covers slightly more, so the count can drop a little.
Does a diagonal layout need more tile?

Yes. Laying tiles at 45 degrees means every row ends in an angled cut at the wall, and many of those offcuts cannot be reused. Plan on about 15% waste for diagonal or herringbone layouts instead of the usual 10% for a straight grid layout.
Do I count grout lines when calculating tile?

Yes, and they work in your favor. Each tile plus its grout gap, often 1/8 inch (3 mm), covers a slightly larger footprint than the tile alone, so a wider gap slightly reduces the number of tiles needed. The effect is small with large tiles but noticeable with small subway tile.
